message.abstract: BARD1 (BRCA1-associated RING domain 1) is a moderate-penetrance breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility gene, yet the majority of missense variants identified through clinical genetic testing remain classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in ClinVar. Unlike BRCA1, ATM, and RAD51C, no published study has systematically integrated multiple orthogonal in silico pathogenicity predictors across the full BARD1 missense VUS set stratified by population frequency. We retrieved all BARD1 missense VUS from ClinVar (n = 1,891), annotated each variant using Ensembl VEP with the REVEL, CADD, and AlphaMissense plugins, and cross-referenced gnomAD exome and genome allele frequencies. Variants were mapped onto three functional domains (RING, ankyrin repeat [ANK], and tandem BRCT) using established domain boundaries. We identified 290 variants (15.3%) for which all three predictors concordantly indicated a damaging effect, and 170 of these were both absent from gnomAD and located within a functional domain, forming a high-priority reclassification candidate set. This set was enriched in the ANK and BRCT domains (63 and 78 variants respectively) relative to RING (29 variants). Several top-ranked candidates, including p.Asp458 substitutions, converge with residues independently identified as functionally critical in a recent saturation genome editing study of the BARD1 ANK-BRCT nucleosome-binding interface. These findings nominate a defined subset of BARD1 VUS as priorities for functional validation and clinical reclassification.
title: Computational Prioritization of BARD1 Missense Variants of Uncertain Significance Using Integrated REVEL, CADD, and AlphaMissense Predictions with gnomAD Population Frequency Stratification
